thread:
Anya: Heads-up — offsite in two weeks. Quick question: who brings a full toiletry/shave kit vs just a tiny travel kit and buys razors/shampoo there? Trying to avoid checked luggage. Also: hairdryer — bring or trust hotel?

Lee: I always bring a tiny electric razor and a small bottle of shampoo. Hotels usually have a hairdryer but they’re meh. :shrug:

Carlos: Buy local if you have space constraints. Razors are cheap everywhere. But I carry a small travel toothbrush + toothpaste.

Tess: Hotel dryers are hit or miss. If you care about blowouts, bring a mini dryer or plan to air-dry. For shaving: single-use razors in carry-on ok if in sealed pack.

Anya: Good tips. Anyone bring shaving cream foam in carry-on? TSA liquid limits are annoying.

Lee: I use shave soap bars — solid, no liquid drama. Lasts forever, super light. 10/10 recommend.

Carlos: Sample-size aerosols are technically allowed but risky. I do a simple checklist instead:

```
- toothbrush (solid)
- shave soap / razor (sealed)
- solid sunscreen stick
- travel deodorant (solid)
- tiny cologne sample (optional)
```

Tess: Vote: bring hairdryer (+1) vs buy at hotel (:+1: is bring, :raised_hand: is buy). I put +1 in case we need speed-dry before dinners.

Lee: :+1: (bringing compact dryer)

Carlos: :raised_hand: (trust hotel)

Anya: Ok looks like mixed. Final q — adapters: universal adapter or plug-on USB brick? 

Tess: USB brick with 2 USB-C ports covers most phone/laptop/airtag needs. Add a cheap universal adapter only if you have weird plugs.

flights-bot: Reminder: checked bag fees vary by carrier. If you decide to check for toiletries, compare fees first: https://example.com/checked-bag-rates

Anya: Thanks all — leaning towards travel solids + USB brick, maybe toss a mini dryer if I can squeeze it. Appreciate the quick input! :heart:
